service_liquidation_page_title: Company dissolution and liquidation of an s.r.o.
service_liquidation_intro_title: Closing a limited liability company is a multi-stage process
service_liquidation_intro_text: Dissolving an s.r.o. is not a one-time action, but a sequence of steps that must be completed in the correct order and properly documented. An incorrectly conducted liquidation may result in the company ceasing its actual operations while still legally existing and continuing to incur obligations (filing tax returns, penalties for inactivity).
service_liquidation_when_title: When is liquidation required and when is another procedure sufficient?
service_liquidation_when_text: If the company has no assets or liabilities, in some cases it may be possible to use a simpler procedure to remove the company from the register without liquidation. However, in most situations where the company owns assets, has receivables or obligations towards third parties, proper liquidation is required — only after it has been completed can an application for removal from the Commercial Register be submitted.
service_liquidation_phase_1_text: The general meeting (or sole shareholder) adopts a decision to enter liquidation and appoints a liquidator.
service_liquidation_phase_2_text: The entry into liquidation is recorded in the Commercial Register and published so that potential creditors can submit their claims.
service_liquidation_phase_3_text: The liquidator prepares the opening liquidation balance sheet, realises the company's assets, satisfies creditors' claims and settles receivables.
service_liquidation_phase_4_title: Completion of tax and accounting matters
service_liquidation_phase_4_text: Submission of the tax return as of the date of preparation of the application for removal, final settlement with the tax office, social security administration and health insurance company.
service_liquidation_phase_5_title: Application for removal from the register
service_liquidation_phase_5_text: After the liquidation has been completed and any liquidation balance has been distributed among the shareholders, an application is submitted to remove the company from the Commercial Register.
service_liquidation_duration_text: The law sets a minimum period (usually several months) from the publication of the entry into liquidation, during which creditors can submit their claims. The total duration depends on the complexity of the company's financial situation — the process is usually faster for simple companies without debts or assets, while companies with unresolved liabilities or receivables require more time.

service_liquidation_experts_title: Why entrust the liquidation to professionals
service_liquidation_experts_text: Liquidation involves legal, accounting and tax matters simultaneously, and an error in any of these areas can prolong the process or expose the company to the risk of penalties. We handle the entire process — from appointing the liquidator and maintaining liquidation accounting to the final removal from the register — so that the closure of the business is completed properly and without unnecessary complications.
licenses_intro_title: Do you need a trade licence for your business?
licenses_intro_text: We will help you choose the right type of trade licence, prepare the required documents and handle the notification or concession application.
license_free_text: For most common business activities. A professional qualification is not required for a free trade license; it is sufficient to meet the general requirements and submit an application.
license_craft_text: For activities where professional qualifications or appropriate education and practical experience are required.
license_bound_subtitle: For activities requiring specific professional qualifications
license_bound_text: For certain professional activities, it is necessary to demonstrate the required qualifications, education or professional experience.
license_concession_text: These activities require a concession, i.e. special state authorization. For some activities, proof of professional qualifications or approval from the relevant authority may also be required.

questions_description: We provide clear and structured support at every stage of our cooperation. Below you will find answers to the most common questions about our services and doing business in the Czech Republic.
faq_q1: How long does company registration in the Czech Republic take?
faq_a1: From signing the founding documents to the registration in the Commercial Register, it usually takes between 3 and 15 working days. The speed depends on the selected licences, the amount of registered capital, consent to the company's registered office address, and the readiness of the future directors' documents.
faq_q2: What is the minimum registered capital required for a company?
faq_a2: Under Czech law, a limited liability company can be established with a minimum contribution of CZK 1 per shareholder. In practice, we recommend considering a higher capital amount, as this can increase confidence among suppliers and business partners. If the registered capital is up to CZK 20,000, there is no need to open a special bank account and the company registration process can be faster.
faq_q3: Do I need permanent residence or Czech citizenship to establish a company?
faq_a3: No. A foreigner can establish a company in the Czech Republic without permanent residence. However, the company must have a registered office in the Czech Republic and the requirements for the director must be met, including, for example, proof of a clean criminal record from the country of permanent residence.
faq_q4: What is needed to establish a company?
faq_a4: The basic package includes the founding agreement, a document confirming the company's registered office, proof of the director's clean criminal record, and confirmation of payment of the registered capital. In addition, the appropriate authorisations for business activities must be obtained and the company must be registered with the tax office and other relevant institutions.
faq_q5: Can you help me choose the appropriate legal form of business?
faq_a5: Yes. We will advise you on what is most suitable for your situation — establishing a limited liability company, becoming a sole trader, or choosing another legal form, depending on the planned scale of your business, the number of co-owners, and the level of risk you are prepared to bear with your personal assets.
faq_q6: Is my company required to keep double-entry accounting, or is tax records sufficient?
faq_a6: This depends on the legal form and scale of the business. Commercial companies, such as limited liability companies, are generally required by law to keep full double-entry accounting, while individual entrepreneurs may, under certain conditions, use simplified tax records. We will assess what applies to your particular situation.
faq_q7: Do you provide accounting services for a newly established company with a small turnover?
faq_a7: Yes. We work with both new entrepreneurs and established companies. We adapt the scope and cost of our services to the current size and needs of your business, and as your company grows, the terms of cooperation can change accordingly.
faq_a8: Documents can be sent as scanned copies or uploaded to a shared cloud storage. The frequency and format of document submission are agreed individually, depending on what is most convenient for you.
faq_q9: Who is responsible for accounting errors or a late tax return?
faq_a9: If an error occurs on our side, we take responsibility for it and arrange the necessary correction. At the same time, we value timely and complete information from the client, as meeting deadlines is not always possible without documents being provided sufficiently in advance.
faq_q10: Do you also handle payroll and personnel administration?
faq_a10: Yes. In addition to accounting, we provide payroll calculation, employee registration with the relevant authorities, working-time records and related personnel administration, so you do not have to handle these matters yourself.
faq_q11: What type of trade licence do I need for my business activity?
faq_a11: It depends on the type of activity you plan to carry out. In the Czech Republic, there are free, craft, regulated and concession trades. We will help you determine which licence you need and prepare the required documents.
faq_q12: What is the difference between a free, craft, regulated and concession trade?
faq_a12: A free trade does not require proof of professional qualifications, while craft and certain regulated trades require specific professional qualifications. A concession trade requires a state permit — a concession. We will help you choose the appropriate type based on your planned business activity.
faq_q13: Do I need professional qualifications to obtain a trade licence?
faq_a13: Not always. Professional qualifications are generally not required for a free trade. For craft and certain regulated trades, however, you must provide evidence of the required education, professional experience or other qualifications.
faq_q14: Can you arrange the trade licence for me?
faq_a14: Yes. We will prepare the necessary documents, help you choose the appropriate trade licences and arrange the submission of the application or notification to the relevant Trade Licensing Office.
